artifacts.description: Quartus Prime Pro EDA netlist export (Version 26.1.0 Build 110 03/26/2026 SC Pro Edition)

assumptions.description: Each link is 'this register's next state depends on exactly one bit of kreg', modulo whatever else the cone reads -- a round-key operand, a load path, a mode select. The recovered map is therefore the map the design applies in the operating mode where the source reaches the register, not an unconditional wire permutation. A pure-wire map, when one exists, is reported separately as hal_crypto/permutation/layer, which is the stronger claim.

76 of the 80 bits link back to kreg; the other 4 read more than one bit of it or none, so they are not claimed. Only a single consistent rotation amount is reported from a partial map -- a general permutation cannot be extrapolated from one.
tennm_lcell_comb and tennm_ff behave as documented in hal_agilex.primitives, which was validated by simulating real Quartus exports against the RTL they were synthesised from.
The .vo reader refuses Verilog it does not understand, so no instance can have been dropped silently before the analysis ran.

The cone walk stops at every vector the export declares that is at least 4 bits wide, so 'kreg' is the layer named in the netlist. A synthesiser that dissolved that vector would leave this map unrecoverable -- which is a fact about the export, not about the design.

bounds.description: a statement about the next-state functions, each evaluated exhaustively over the cut described below

method.description: Enumerates the whole input space of a combinational cone using only the tennm_lcell_comb semantics in hal_agilex.primitives, and reads the truth table off it. Exhaustive, so the resulting table is the function, not a sample of it.
method.name: exhaustive cone evaluation

findings.summary: 76 of the 80 bits of register bank kreg have a next-state cone that reads exactly one bit of kreg, and the index map is a rotation left by 61. The cones were enumerated over their whole input space, so 'reads exactly one bit' is read off the function and not off the wiring -- which is the point: every link here passes through a cell with other operands (at most 4 other net(s) per link, 2 of them shared by every link), so the wiring tier sees nothing at all. This is the weaker claim of the two: it says which bit each register reads, not that the map is the wiring. The links are gated, not pure XORs: the source bit reaches the register in one operating mode of the side inputs, which is what a parallel load or an enable looks like after synthesis.
findings.title: register bank kreg reads kreg rotated left by 61, recovered from the next-state cone support

findings.summary: 64 of the 64 bits of register bank state have a next-state cone that reads exactly one bit of subs, and the index map is a general permutation. The cones were enumerated over their whole input space, so 'reads exactly one bit' is read off the function and not off the wiring -- which is the point: every link here passes through a cell with other operands (at most 6 other net(s) per link, 2 of them shared by every link), so the wiring tier sees nothing at all. This is the weaker claim of the two: it says which bit each register reads, not that the map is the wiring. It equals the published present_player. The links are gated, not pure XORs: the source bit reaches the register in one operating mode of the side inputs, which is what a parallel load or an enable looks like after synthesis.
findings.title: A 64-bit general bit map from subs into register bank state, recovered from the next-state cone support matching present_player

method.description: Walks the netlist graph produced by hal_agilex.vo_netlist: register chains, carry chains, pure-wire bit maps and LUT cones. No solver and no simulation.
method.name: structural crypto pattern match

findings.summary: Every pure-wire map between two equally wide vectors is the identity, so there is no permutation layer to compare against the published pLayers. 2 map(s) were recovered from the next-state cone support instead and are reported separately: the silence here is about wires, not about the design.
findings.title: No non-identity bit permutation layer
